name: pteranodon
_about: PTERANODON LONGICEPS (2026-11-06, gen: scratchpad sc/ptero/gen.py): a male, 5.95 m across the wings, a turkey's body under them -- a compact deep furred trunk (pycnofibres: pale grey-cream, darker over the back) broad over the flight muscles, a short stout neck held in a gentle S, and a head longer than the trunk: one laterally flattened wedge, the long straight toothless beak running back into the skull and on into the flat crest, as long again. STANDING (the rest pose) on all fours on the folded wings: the metacarpal the front leg, the three free clawed fingers on the ground ahead, the wing finger folded back tight up the metacarpal and along the forearm, its skin furled beside the bones in pleated strips, and the inner wing hanging from the humerus and elbow in a slack fold of skin down over the flank onto the thigh and knee; IN FLIGHT (flyRot) long narrow wings, the trailing edge from the pointed tip in to the ankles, the legs spread behind; on the upstroke the hand flexes back at the wrist (flyUp). Its skin is one membrane each side (bodymesh.js membraneMesh), every free chord furled on a bone of its own (2026-11-08, fold) THE FOLDED WING READS AS SKIN: the forearm's chords and the wing finger's furl to half the gap between the two bones (up to 20 cm, every other one 0.6 of that: pleats), so the folded finger carries a broad pleated web that meets the forearm's -- the brachiopatagium bunched between arm and finger, not a strip -- and the inner wing hangs from the humerus and elbow down to the shin (PT_LEGS .85); aloft unchanged. SHARP PASS 2 (2026-11-08): the pointed parts -- toeClaw, wDigAClaw, wDigBClaw, wDigCClaw (7 in all) -- are the engine's sharp `horn`s (sharp.js), made from the field shapes they replaced by tools/creaturegen/sharp/ (claws.py, teeth.py, spikes.py, antlers.py, bills.py): rooted in the body, tips pointed; RE-RUN those after this species' generator. (2026-11-08, review.py: claws) The claws RE-ROOTED (review.py): each a sheath as wide as the claw where it leaves the toe, sunk in it, the join faired (horn `fair`: grown out of the skin in its paint), darker at the base fading to its own colour at the point -- no pale cut edge where it leaves the fur.
